parts.latex: A sector with perimeter 28 cm contains an angle of 1.5 radians at the centre of a circle with radius $r$ cm. What is the value of $r$?
Consider the functions $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=x+2$. Which of the following expressions is equal to $f(g(x))-g(f(x))$?

A and B are two independent events with $P(A\cup B)=\dfrac{3}{8}$ and $P(A)=\dfrac{1}{4}$.

What is the value of $P(B)$?
What is the domain of the function $f(x)=\ln(x-1)+\sqrt{2-x}$?
The function $f(x)=e^x$ is transformed into the function $g(x)=e^{x+2}$. Which of the following describes the effect of this transformation?
Which of the following is an expression for $\dfrac{d}{dx}\log_{10}3x$?

The marks on a test are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

2.5% of the marks are 34 or less and 16% of the marks are 70 or more. What is the value of $\mu$?
Which of the following is an expression for $\displaystyle\int\left(\dfrac{1}{1+\sin x}+\dfrac{1}{1-\sin x}\right)dx$?
A single lump sum investment of $\$P$ earns an amount of interest $\$I$ after 2 years with a rate of interest of 6% p.a. compounded monthly. Which of the following is an expression for $P$?

If $x>0$ what is the limiting sum of the series

$\log_2 x-\log_4 x+\log_{16}x-\log_{256}x+\dots+(-1)^{n+1}\log_{2^{\left(2^{n-1}\right)}}x+\dots$ ?
A circle has equation $x^2+y^2-6x+4y+k=0$ for some constant $k$. Find the set of possible values of $k$.
If $\tan x=3$ and $\sin x<0$ find the exact value of $\cos x$.
$A(-1,-5)$ and $B(5,-1)$ are two points. Find in general form the equation of the straight line through the midpoint of $AB$ and perpendicular to $AB$.
Find the coordinates of the point on the curve $y=2\sqrt{x}$ where the tangent to the curve is parallel to the line $2x-y-2=0$.

If the second ball is red, a third ball is chosen at random without replacement from the remaining balls.

questions.stem_latex: At the Oztown school, HSC Trial marks in English Standard had a mean of 72 and a standard deviation of 8, whilst HSC Trial marks in Mathematics Standard 2 had a mean of 68 and a standard deviation of 10.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Otto scored 66 in the English Standard Trial and 63 in the Mathematics Standard 2 Trial. Explain which of these was Otto's better performance.

parts.label: b

Find the value of the constant $k>0$ such that $\displaystyle\int_{\ln k}^{\ln k^2}\left(1+\dfrac{1}{x}\right)dx=\ln 10$.
Find the coordinates and nature of the stationary points on the curve $y=\dfrac{x^2}{x-2}$.

questions.stem_latex: At time $t$ hours after midnight on a particular day the depth $D$ metres of water in the Oztown harbour is given by the function $D=8+2\cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{25}t\right)$ for $0\le t\le 24$.

parts.label: b

questions.stem_latex: An item is purchased for \$20 000. It appreciates in value so that after $t$ years its value $\$V$ is given by the formula $V=20000p^t$ for some constant $p>1$. After 9 years its value is \$32 000.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find the value of $p$ correct to 4 decimal places.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find correct to the nearest \$10 per year the rate at which the item is appreciating in value after 9 years.

questions.stem_latex: At the start of year 2000 a colony of 600 animals was established in a sanctuary. Each year the population size grows at a rate of 10% per year and at the end of each year 50 of the animals are released into the wild. The population size $P_n$ at the end of the $n^{\text{th}}$ year can be determined using the recurrence relation $P_n=1.1\times P_{n-1}-50$ where $n=1,2,3,\dots$ and $P_0=600$.

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Write down expressions for $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$ in terms of $P_0$ and hence show that

$P_n=100\times(1.1)^n+500$.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the year in which the growth in population size from the beginning of that year to the start of the next year first exceeds 100.

questions.stem_latex: A particle is moving in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds it has displacement $x$ metres from a fixed point $O$ on the line and velocity $v=3\sqrt{t+1}-9$ metres per second. Initially the particle is at $O$.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Use integration to show that $x=2(t+1)\sqrt{t+1}-9t-2$.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find when and where the particle is at rest.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Find the distance travelled by the particle in the first 24 seconds of its motion.

questions.stem_latex: The cost $\$C$ per hour when employees work $x$ hours per day to complete a project is given by $C=ax^3+d$ for some constants $a$ and $d$. The time $T$ hours to complete the project is given by $T=\dfrac{120}{x}$. In order to complete the project, the cost would be \$248 per hour when employees work 4 hours per day on the project and \$472 per hour when employees work 8 hours per day on the project.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Write down two equations in $a$ and $d$ and solve these equations to find the values of $a$ and $d$.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Show that the total cost $\$S$ of completing the project when employees work $x$ hours per day on the project is given by $S=60x^2+\dfrac{25\,920}{x}$.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Use differentiation to find the minimum total cost of completing the project.

questions.stem_latex:

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Show that $f(x)$ is a probability density function.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ of the random variable $X$.

solutions.latex:
$y=\dfrac{x^2}{x-2}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2x(x-2)-x^2}{(x-2)^2}=\dfrac{x^2-4x}{(x-2)^2}=\dfrac{x(x-4)}{(x-2)^2}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow x=0,\ y=0$ or $x=4,\ y=8$

Stationary points are $(0,0)$ and $(4,8)$.

Sign of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$: positive for $x<0$, zero at $x=0$, negative for $0<x<2$ and $2<x<4$, zero at $x=4$, positive for $x>4$ (discontinuity at $x=2$).

$(0,0)$ is a maximum turning point. $(4,8)$ is a minimum turning point

Area is given by $\displaystyle\int_{\ln2}^{\ln4}\left(6-8e^{-x}-e^x\right)dx=\left[6x+8e^{-x}-e^x\right]_{\ln2}^{\ln4}$

$=6(\ln4-\ln2)+8\left(e^{-\ln4}-e^{-\ln2}\right)-\left(e^{\ln4}-e^{\ln2}\right)$

$=6\ln2+8\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)-(4-2)$

$=6\ln2-4$

Hence area is $(6\ln2-4)$ sq. units.
